title: Location fix
description:
A single geographic position reported by the location module. Carried as the `payload` of an observation envelope; the envelope's `observed_at` is the time of the fix, so this payload carries no timestamp of its own.

Raw location traces are among the most re-identifying data a study can hold -- a handful of points is often enough to identify a person -- so this contract is built around making data minimisation explicit rather than optional. `generalization` records what precision reduction was deliberately applied, and `region_only` studies can report coarse geography with no coordinates at all.
$comment: The critical distinction here is between `accuracy_m` (how well the device could locate itself -- a sensor limitation) and `generalization` (how much precision the study chose to discard -- a policy decision). Conflating them makes both uninterpretable: you can no longer tell a poor urban-canyon GPS fix from a deliberately coarsened one, and you cannot reason about either measurement error or disclosure risk.

latitude.description: Decimal degrees, WGS84. Null or absent only when generalization.method is 'region_only'.

accuracy_m.description: Horizontal accuracy radius in metres as reported by the platform (68% confidence). A sensor property, not a privacy control. Required whenever coordinates are present: a fix without an accuracy estimate cannot be quality-filtered, and unfiltered fixes silently corrupt mobility measures.

generalization.description: What deliberate precision reduction was applied on-device before upload. Always present, including when nothing was reduced, so that a dataset is self-describing and two studies with different minimisation policies can be told apart without consulting their protocols.

method.description: none = full precision as measured; truncated = decimal places dropped; grid = snapped to a grid cell centre; geohash = reduced to a geohash prefix; region_only = no coordinates, coarse geography only.

decimals.description: Decimal places retained when method is 'truncated'.

cell_size_m.description: Grid cell edge length in metres when method is 'grid'.

geohash.description: The geohash itself when method is 'geohash'. Base32, standard geohash alphabet.

region.description: Coarse geography, typically derived on-device by reverse geocoding. Reporting region without coordinates is the minimal-disclosure mode used by studies that only need country-level context, as Travel Healthy does for travel notices.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. A code rather than a name: reverse geocoders return names in the device locale, which silently breaks cross-site joins.

geocoder.description: Which geocoder produced this, since different geocoders disagree at borders.

speed_mps.description: Ground speed in metres per second.

heading_deg.description: Direction of travel in degrees clockwise from true north.

provider.description: How the position was obtained. Accuracy characteristics differ sharply between providers, so mixing them without recording which was used makes a mobility dataset hard to interpret.

sample_source.description: What caused this fix to be recorded. Essential for completeness analysis: a gap during 'background' sampling means something different from a gap when the app was never opened.

geofence_id.description: The geofence that triggered this fix, when sample_source is 'geofence'. Links a location observation to a JITAI decision point.

is_moving.description: Platform's moving/stationary determination at the time of the fix.

battery_level.description: Battery fraction at the time of the fix. Recorded because battery state explains most long gaps in background location data, and a completeness metric that cannot distinguish 'participant disengaged' from 'phone was dead' is not measuring engagement.

mock_location.description: Platform flag indicating the fix came from a mock location provider. Retained as an integrity signal: in incentivised or compensated studies, spoofed location is a real and otherwise invisible failure mode.
